bull_bear.body: Geopolitical: Prolonged Middle East conflict impacting global economy/energy prices. Regulatory: Delays in Canada municipal permits for expansion. Sectoral: Textile industry cyclicality (though currently reviving). Execution: Conversion of Green Hydrogen MOUs to firm orders.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and forward-looking; Emphasizes 'best years ahead' despite macro headwinds; Defensive on margin queries citing continuous improvement; Transparent about one-time accounting hits; Aggressive on order book growth narrative.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Revenue/Backlog Mismatch: Backlog includes 100% value of indirect sales while revenue books only commission, artificially depressing asset turnover ratios if not adjusted. Export Safety: 100% of export receivables covered by Letters of Credit, nullifying Bangladesh geopolitical risk exposure. Fan Division: Hidden capacity jump of 40% not fully reflected in top-line yet due to mix.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt to equity of 0.28x as at March 2026; Quickmill is separately described as "Net Debt Free with adequate surplus".
- Consolidated balance sheet shows total equity rising 155, 225, 232 Rs Cr over FY24-FY26, with long term borrowings 63, 60, 64 Rs Cr and short term borrowings 27, 22, 16 Rs Cr.
- The Penta acquisition was structured to stagger cash outflow - 80% (INR 15.84 Cr) at closing and the 20% balance spread over five annual payments beginning Apr 2027.
- The deck makes no statement on dividend policy or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing franchise: incorporated in 1941 and described as a leader among engineering companies, with 82 years of continuity as a listed engineering house
- Technology access through both in-house development and collaboration with leading engineering companies worldwide
- Agency-house model representing reputed overseas principals from Czech Republic, Belgium, Italy, Germany, South Korea, China and Taiwan alongside own manufactured machines
- Turnkey project capability as engineers and contractors, executed both in India and internationally
- Nationwide pre-sales and post-sales service through a dedicated engineering team and a network of multiple offices across the country
- EEG has in-house capabilities of providing 100% Make in India solutions across steel, power, oil & gas, sugar, cement and solar manufacturing industries
- Textile Machinery Group retained overall market share and average business volume despite high demand and raw-material price volatility, via product portfolio expansion and wider geographic reach through key representations
- Machine Tool Manufacturing improved market share on the back of better quality and more new CNC models
- Cordial and pro-active industrial relations with employees at all levels including the union
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global and domestic demand-supply swings that move selling prices of finished goods — The Board's cautionary statement names demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices of finished goods as the first factor that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements - for a capital-goods maker with no pricing power over cyclical customer capex, this is the primary earnings swing factor.
- Input availability and input prices — Explicitly flagged in the cautionary statement; the Company converts bought-out material and components into machinery, so availability gaps or price spikes compress margins between order booking and execution.
- Changes in government regulations and tax laws — Named as a factor that could influence operations. The year already carried a concrete instance of this exposure: the exceptional item mainly comprised a non-cash charge due to the introduction of the New Labour Code.
- Economic and political developments in the overseas markets where the Company operates — The cautionary statement covers economic developments in India and in countries in which the Company conducts business; the Company runs a manufacturing subsidiary in Peterborough, Canada (Quickmill Inc.) selling globally into Energy, Heat Transfer, Steel Service, large industrial machinery and job shop sectors, so a meaningful share of the consolidated business is exposed to non-Indian cycles and currency.
- Litigation — Listed among the factors that could influence operations. As at the reporting date, however, no significant or material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals affecting going-concern status, and no application has been made under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
- Industrial relations — Named in the cautionary statement as an incidental factor that could influence operations; the Company runs unionised manufacturing facilities, so a breakdown in industrial relations would directly interrupt production.
- Concentration of consolidated earnings in subsidiaries outside the standalone entity — The Directors' Report shows the standalone entity in loss before tax for the year while the consolidated result stayed in profit, meaning subsidiary operations - Quickmill Inc., Canada and the newly incorporated Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited - carry a disproportionate share of group profitability and any setback there would be felt directly.
- Execution risk in a newly incorporated business line — Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited was only incorporated in April 2025 and is engaged in Water Effluent Treatment Plant and Zero Liquid Discharge work for industries - an unproven vertical whose track record is a single part year.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "A Well Diversified Business Group" with six business segments: Air Engineering, Textile Machinery, Machine Tools, Robotics & Factory Automation (Penta), Environmental Engineering, and Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Pvt Ltd (water/effluent treatment).
- Stated USPs: "Diverse Business Segments, Extensive marketing network, Large Manufacturing Base, A Growing Orderbook, Focus on High Growth Business".
- Export reach is stated two ways in the same deck: "Exports in 20+ Countries" on the at-a-glance slide, versus "Number of country exports: Over 15" on the distribution-network slide.
- Machine Tools is both a manufacturer and an agency/trading house - it represents third-party metal cutting, metal forming and workshop machine packages, and is an agent for leading spinning, knitting, processing and technical textile machinery brands.
- Quickmill (Peterborough, Ontario) manufactures large-size gantry drilling & milling machines for energy, structural steel, aviation, large equipment and job-shop sectors, with "105 Satisfied Clients", "400+ Projects Installed", "130+ Customers Worldwide" and FANUC America Authorized CNC Aggregator status.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Penta Automation was bought from Manders Industries B.V., Netherlands (49%) and founders Mr. Dharmesh Mistry & Ms. Avani Mistry (51%); post-completion Penta becomes a Batliboi subsidiary and Pats Robotics an indirect subsidiary via Penta. Penta revenue is stated at Rs 25.17 Cr in FY26 and the acquisition is described as "earnings-accretive".
- [Guidance] Management reiterates FY27 guidance of "~10% sustainable topline growth with stable margins"; BREPL is given a "Projected Growth Potential:- 12%-15% CAGR".
- [Major order] Environmental Engineering secured a contract from SAEL Industries Ltd. valued at Rs 52 Cr for design, supply, installation and commissioning of a pollution system for its upcoming Solar Cell Manufacturing facility at Jewar, Uttar Pradesh - described as a milestone in Batliboi's foray into the solar energy sector.
- [Client base] Penta's blue-chip clientele includes Bosch, Siemens, ABB, ZF India, Valeo, Yazaki, Schneider Electric, SKF, Schaeffler, L&T, TE Connectivity and Knorr-Bremse (30+ global Tier-1/Tier-2 manufacturers); Batliboi's own listed customers span JSW Steel, L&T, SAIL, BARC, ISRO's Space Applications Centre, Trident, Welspun, Arcelor Mittal/Nippon Steel and Adani group.
- [Third-party market sizing] The deck cites external forecasts it does not own: global CNC machines market ~USD 74bn (2024) to ~USD 187.2bn by 2034 at 9.8% CAGR (market.us); global industrial robotics USD 54bn (FY22) to USD 94bn (FY29) (Mordor Intelligence); India waste water treatment USD 5bn (FY22) to USD 11bn (FY29) at 12% CAGR; India-UK FTA seen spurring 13% CAGR in textile exports with a PLI outlay of Rs 10,683 Cr.
- [Macro caveat] Management conditions its FY27 confidence on "Not with standing any further adverse impact, if any, on the global and Indian economy in the event of a prolonged conflict in the middle east and a stable tariff regime".
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Batliboi manufactures, engineers, contracts and markets advanced machinery from plants in Surat (India) and Peterborough (Canada), with product designs developed in-house or in collaboration with leading engineering companies worldwide. Its operations span the Machine Tool Group (CNC and conventional metal-cutting/metal-forming machines, plus an agency-house trading business representing overseas principals), the Textile Engineering Group (Air Engineering humidification and waste-collection plant, and Textile Machinery for spinning, knitting and processing), and the Environmental Engineering Group (air pollution control equipment, industrial fans and green hydrogen projects). Customers are served through corporate-level Business Groups backed by a dedicated engineering team providing pre-sales and post-sales service via a network of multiple offices across the country.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Use the Employee Stock Option Plan as a retention and alignment tool: after a long gap, three fresh grant lots (10th, 11th and 12th) were made in FY2025-26 to divisional and functional leadership across Machine Tool Manufacturing and Foundry, Machine Tool Trading, Air Engineering, Textile Machinery, Environmental Engineering and corporate finance, with options vesting in three instalments after 36, 48 and 60 months from grant.
- Maintain an annual, externally validated safety and compliance discipline - safety audit conducted once a year by an independent consultant as a matter of Company practice, alongside an equal-opportunity workplace policy covering permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees.
- Run a proactive, framework-based risk management approach in which risks in the internal and external environment are assessed, monitored, evaluated and mitigated rather than handled reactively.
- Dividend is recommended annually by the Board on both equity and preference capital and is paid only after approval by members at the Annual General Meeting; for the year under review a final equity dividend plus the contracted 1% and 8% preference dividends were recommended subject to that approval. The year's result is taken directly to Retained Earnings rather than appropriated to a separate reserve. Share issuance is kept narrow and purpose-bound: during the year equity and preference shares were issued only to give effect to the NCLT-sanctioned Scheme of Amalgamation of Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited, and equity was issued on exercise of employee stock options; apart from these, no shares with differential rights as to dividend or voting, and no sweat equity shares, were issued. Employee ownership is used as a deliberate retention lever - the Company operates an Employee Stock Option Plan approved by members in December 2011 with a view to encourage, reward and retain employees and to give them an opportunity to participate in the growth of the Company, administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, which also grants the options. The Company maintains an active investor-servicing discipline, including measures to reduce the quantum of unclaimed dividends and to ensure timely receipt of dividend warrants by shareholders.
- Annual independent safety audit: as a matter of Company practice a safety audit is conducted once a year, and for the year under review it was conducted by an Independent Consultant.
- Prevention of sexual harassment: a POSH policy covering all permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees is in place with a constituted Internal Complaint Committee, and the policy is published on the Company's website; no complaints were received during 2025-2026 and none were pending for more than 90 days.
- Equal-opportunity workplace: the Company states it is an equal opportunity employer and consciously strives to build a work culture that promotes the dignity of all employees.
- Maternity benefit compliance: the Company has complied with the provisions relating to the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended from time to time.
- Board-level risk management framework: an adequate risk management framework capable of addressing risks is in place, under which risks in the internal and external environment are assessed, monitored, evaluated and mitigated proactively.
- Internal financial control: the Audit Committee has established and maintained an effective Internal Control over financial reporting, with standard operating practices laid down, followed and independently audited.
- Clean audit and fraud record: the statutory audit report for 2025-2026 contains no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and no frauds were reported by the statutory auditors under Section 143(12).
- Unclaimed dividend stewardship: as on 31st March 2026 the Company had no unpaid dividend due for transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund, and the list of dividends previously transferred to IEPF is published on the Company's website.
- Environmental engineering as a business line: the group's subsidiary Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited is engaged in Water Effluent Treatment Plant and Zero Liquid Discharge solutions for industries, aligning a revenue stream with industrial water-pollution abatement.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Batliboi's FY2025-26 expansion effort was concentrated at the Udhna manufacturing facilities and in energy self-sufficiency. Capital expenditure in the foundry and machine shop was completed during FY25-26 with the aim of increasing production, improving productivity and quality and reducing cost; combined with ongoing redesign and modification of machines based on customer and competitive feedback, this resulted in production rising by around 30% compared with the prior fiscal. In the foundry, a new energy-efficient induction furnace of 6T capacity was commissioned, delivering power savings of about 21%. On renewable self-generation, installation of an 800 kW roof-top solar plant is underway and will be commissioned in the first quarter of FY26-27, and the Company plans to add a further 400 kW of solar in FY26-27; combined savings from solar and the existing windmill are expected to reduce power cost, and LED lighting continues to be rolled out through the shop and assembly areas as an ongoing process. The product basket is being widened through design-stage work on a smaller version of the Vertical Turning Lathe and a large-size Vertical Machining Center, while the Air Engineering Group has completed a set of shop-floor and product improvements (new geared motor and door for the screen filter, new impellers for semi-central units, a dust-proof area for finished goods, a dock leveler for export container loading and epoxy flooring for the shop). At the Canadian subsidiary Quickmill, High Rail machine development continues and development of a new HD Rail machine has started. Structurally, the Scheme of Amalgamation merging Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited with and into Batliboi Limited was given effect during the year following the NCLT Mumbai order, with equity shares allotted on 24th June 2025 and 8% redeemable preference shares on 23rd March 2026 to the transferor company's shareholders.

deepdive.thesis: Batliboi closed FY26 with a record order backlog of INR 593 Cr (+75% YoY) and INR 990 Cr inflows, signaling strong FY27 revenue visibility despite FY26 PAT being suppressed to INR 7 Cr by one-time labor code provisions and merger accounting. The strategic pivot toward high-margin environmental engineering (ZLD/Green Hydrogen) and expanded CNC product baskets offers a clear path to operating leverage and margin expansion beyond the current ~7% levels.

open.item: Machine Tool Manufacturing expects to keep growing at a pace similar to FY25-26's roughly 30% top-line growth in FY26-27.
The Company plans to add another 400 kW of solar capacity in FY26-27 to further reduce power costs.

Quickmill Inc.'s performance is expected to improve considerably in FY26-27 on the back of healthy pending orders at the start of the year and strong prospects in the pipeline, after profitability came in marginally lower than projected in FY25-26.
The Textile Engineering Group will focus on generating business from the retro-fit segment and export markets such as Africa and South Asia.
Machine Tool Manufacturing is expanding its product range into higher-size vertical machining centres and small-size vertical turning lathes, both aimed at the mould and die industry.
LED lights are installed in the shop and assembly areas and the roll-out continues as an ongoing process, with combined savings from solar and the windmill expected to reduce power cost.
At Quickmill, High Rail machine development continues and development of a new HD Rail machine has been started.
A smaller version of the Vertical Turning Lathe and a large-size Vertical Machining Center are in the design stage to expand the product basket.

Options granted under the Batliboi Stock Option Plan remain to be vested in three instalments 36, 48 and 60 months from the date of grant, with a maximum exercise term of 5 years from vesting - a standing dilution and retention commitment carried forward from the FY2025-26 grants.
EEG flags that the market has become very competitive so maintaining margin is a challenge, with global uncertainty causing fluctuation in steel and other fabrication input prices.
Management flags that the geopolitical situation in the Gulf and any adverse move in crude prices would raise input costs and could slow capex investment by major engineering industries.

Management's planning assumption is that the domestic machine tool market stays robust and grows at a 7 to 8% CAGR, driven by auto and auto components, aerospace, defence, strategic sectors and agriculture - a checkable external claim underpinning the machine tool growth guidance.
Canadian subsidiary Quickmill Inc. is focusing on new business in the Gulf.
EEG is working to keep margins intact through design improvement, alternative vendor development and leveraging bulk buying.
EEG will selectively choose Oil & Gas and Solar industry projects on the basis of profitability and cash flow, while building visibility in the Cement market.

risks.note: The cautionary statement covers economic developments in India and in countries in which the Company conducts business; the Company runs a manufacturing subsidiary in Peterborough, Canada (Quickmill Inc.) selling globally into Energy, Heat Transfer, Steel Service, large industrial machinery and job shop sectors, so a meaningful share of the consolidated business is exposed to non-Indian cycles and currency.
risks.risk: Economic and political developments in the overseas markets where the Company operates

risks.note: Listed among the factors that could influence operations. As at the reporting date, however, no significant or material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals affecting going-concern status, and no application has been made under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.

Named in the cautionary statement as an incidental factor that could influence operations; the Company runs unionised manufacturing facilities, so a breakdown in industrial relations would directly interrupt production.

The Directors' Report shows the standalone entity in loss before tax for the year while the consolidated result stayed in profit, meaning subsidiary operations - Quickmill Inc., Canada and the newly incorporated Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited - carry a disproportionate share of group profitability and any setback there would be felt directly.

meta.thesis: Batliboi closed FY26 with a record order backlog of INR 593 Cr (+75% YoY) and INR 990 Cr inflows, signaling strong FY27 revenue visibility despite FY26 PAT being suppressed to INR 7 Cr by one-time labor code provisions and merger accounting. The strategic pivot toward high-margin environmental engineering (ZLD/Green Hydrogen) and expanded CNC product baskets offers a clear path to operating leverage and margin expansion beyond the current ~7% levels.
